en.title: Méribel powder forecast next week (23–29 November 2026): 28 cm up top
en.description: Méribel's upper slopes collect 28 cm next week (23–29 Nov); most falls Wed–Thu and Sun. Data from 16 Nov.
en.lede: Next week, 23 to 29 November, Méribel's upper slopes gather 28 cm in the middle of our forecast range, with lows of 13 cm and highs of 44 cm. This follows a wet start to the season; the depth builds on what the mountain already holds and brings fresh powder to the high terrain.

p: Méribel's forecast splits into bands by height. At 2700 m, near the top, expect 28 cm (13–44 cm). At 2000 m in the middle of the mountain, 26 cm (12–41 cm). At 1200 m near the base, 19 cm (4–34 cm). The drop from top to base tells you the story: snow turns wetter lower down, so plan your day around the height where the best turns stay dry.

The range widens as height falls, which is normal early in the season when the weather is still unsettled. The middle value gives you a working number; the low and high cases show how much room for change there is.

Three days carry the bulk of next week's snow. Wednesday 25 November brings 9 cm at the top (up to 9 cm in the high case). Thursday 26 adds 8 cm (up to 13 cm). Sunday 29 contributes 6 cm (up to 10 cm). If you can pick one day to ski fresh powder, the morning after Wednesday 25 is your best bet, when 9 cm of new snow will have topped up the upper slopes.
Tuesday and Wednesday morning see lighter falls, so your timing matters. Thursday morning offers a second chance. By Friday to Saturday, the falls ease off, then Sunday brings a final top-up.

The deepest snow next week stays on Mont Vallon and the Saulire ridge. Within Mont Vallon, the north-facing slopes above Mottaret hold the most and stay cold longest as the week wears on. These slopes will offer the softest turns and the slowest melt.

Lower down—the village end of the valley and the runs toward Brides—will see thinner cover and faster softening if any mild air moves in. If the forecast shifts and temperatures climb, these lower zones are where you will notice it first.

sections.h: How it compares: Val Thorens, Courchevel, La Plagne
p: The same storm hits the whole Three Valleys. Val Thorens (10 km away) sees 30 cm at the top next week, Courchevel (5 km away) gets 27 cm, and La Plagne (17 km away) collects 28 cm. Méribel's 28 cm places it in the middle of its nearest neighbours. The differences are small because the system is large and stable across this corner of the Alps.

Snow depth alone should not drive your choice of resort. Terrain shape, which lifts are running, and how crowded the slopes are matter more. Méribel's strength is its size and variety, not a snow advantage over its neighbours this week.

sections.h: Before this week ends: the foundation
p: Before next week even starts, Méribel already holds a substantial snowpack from the week of 17–20 November. The upper slopes collected 86 cm (63–108 cm) during those four days. That layer will act as the base on which next week's 28 cm lands. By 29 November, the total depth up high will be much deeper than the weekly total alone suggests.

The base at 1200 m saw less during 17–20 November (only 6 cm), which underlines the height-dependent nature of this early season: the high peaks have snow; the village level is thinner and more fragile.

A week ahead, the forecast range is wide. The 13–44 cm spread at the top means the system will bring snow, but its exact amount is not yet locked in. The timing of the heaviest falls is more reliable than the total. As each day passes, the picture sharpens; check the daily updates on the resort page.

Watch the weather trend midweek. If mild air arrives instead of cold, the snow line may climb higher, and the lower slopes could turn slushy. If the air stays cold, the whole mountain stays skiable longer.

advice: Target Wednesday 25 November morning or Thursday 26 morning for fresh powder on the upper slopes and Mont Vallon's north-facing slopes above Mottaret.
Before going off-piste, read the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif; fresh snow on a young base carries avalanche risk.
Check the resort's lift opening and status before you travel; snow on the mountain does not guarantee lifts are running early in the season.
Avoid the lower runs toward Brides and the village end of the valley if temperatures warm midweek; these areas see less snow and melt faster.
Watch the forecast each day for changes to the range (13–44 cm at the top); the middle value will shift as new data arrives.
